groups.problem: The test asserts caughtExceptions without joining the reader thread, so an in-flight request can fail after the assertion has already passed.
groups.rationale: All three point to the same race: the assertion runs before the reader thread is joined. All three propose the same fix, which is to keep the thread reference and join it.

groups.problem: deletedAll is set only after every deletion succeeds, so if remove() throws, the non-daemon reader thread keeps running; the stop signal belongs in a finally block.
groups.rationale: Both report the same missing finally block around the deletion loop, which leaves a runaway reader thread when a deletion fails.

problems: The assertion runs without joining the reader thread, so an in-flight request's exception can be added after the assertion passes.
The reader thread may first be scheduled after deletedAll is already true and perform no reads at all, so the test does not exercise concurrency.
uncoveredProblems: The reader thread may not start until deletion is finished, so it may perform no reads and the test would not exercise concurrent access.
